# Lexical structure

Edva source is UTF-8 text with the official `.dva` file extension.
Identifiers follow UAX31: they begin with an alphabetic Unicode character or
`_`, then may contain identifier characters and `_`. The language has no
reserved words; control flow and declarations are formed with operators and
`#` directives.

## Lines and indentation

Indentation starts and ends blocks. Use either spaces everywhere or tabs
everywhere within a source file; mixing them is a syntax error. An indented
block is equivalent to semicolon-separated statements, but a semicolon at the
end of a source line is invalid. Keep lines to 100 characters or fewer.

```dva run
check = value =>
   value > 0
      | "positive"
      | "not positive"
```

Line comments begin with `//`; block comments use `/*` and `*/`.

## Literals

| Kind | Examples | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| integer | `42`, `0xFF`, `0b101`, `0m48`, `0m-16`, `5i16` | explicit widths use a suffix |
| float | `0.5`, `1.0`, `3.0e4` | digits are required on both sides of `.` |
| rune | `'a'`, `'λ'`, `'\n'` | one Unicode scalar value |
| string | `"text\n"` | escaped UTF-8 string |
| here-doc | `"""text"""` | multiline block with margin stripping & interpolation |

`.5`, `1.`, and `3.e4` are not float literals. Unsuffixed integer literals
default to `Int` unless constrained by static type context or an explicit
suffix (`i8`, `i16`, `i32`, `i64`, `u8`, `u16`, `u32`, `u64`).
`#pragma number <type>` changes the default literal type for the rest of its
file; `#pragma number default` restores standard `Int` default mode.

### Here-Docs (`"""..."""`)

Triple-double-quoted strings `"""..."""` define formatted multiline text:
- **Baseline margin stripping**: When the closing `"""` sits on its own line, its column establishes the baseline indentation. That margin is stripped from each content line; any line indented less raises `E1017`.
- **Newline trimming**: Leading newline after `"""` is discarded; line continuation with trailing `\` suppresses newlines.
- **Interpolation**: `${expr}` evaluates expressions directly into the text.
- **Escapes**: `\"""` escapes triple quotes; `\$` escapes interpolation; raw `"` and `""` are literal.

## Tokens and whitespace-sensitive forms

The lexer consumes operators greedily. Keep operator operands separated by
whitespace unless the syntax requires adjacency. In particular, `&builder` is
the unary buffer-address operator, whereas `* value` begins a multiplication
section. Ramification payloads close with `+>` or `->`; a bare `>` is a
comparison operator, not a delimiter.

See [the generated operator table](../../../GRAMMAR.md#16-operators--precedence)
for the complete token inventory and precedence.
